coverage: Premarket, Thu Nov 12 (data through the Tue Nov 10 close)
moodReason: A hotter than expected October CPI pushed Treasury yields toward 5% and raised bets on another Fed rate hike in December, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower on Nov 10. Easing oil prices offer some relief but not enough to change the tone.

stories.headline: October CPI runs hotter than expected on both headline and core prices
stories.what: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core prices rose 0.3% against a 0.2% expectation, the third straight month at that pace. The BLS published no 12-month rate because October 2025 prices were not collected during last year's shutdown; the last annual reading, for September, was 3.7%.
stories.why: Core inflation running above forecast keeps the Fed on a tightening path, which raises discount rates on high-valuation stocks and weighs on the broader market.

stories.headline: Treasury yields climb toward 5% as traders price a December Fed hike
stories.what: The 10-year yield rose to about 4.99% and the 2-year to about 4.69% after the CPI report. Fed funds futures moved toward pricing a near certain rate hike at the December 8 to 9 meeting. Governor Waller leans toward a quarter point hike and said a half point should be considered if core CPI came in around 0.3% or higher.
stories.why: A shift from expected cuts to expected hikes raises borrowing costs across the economy and pulls money away from stocks toward bonds, which pressures valuations.

stories.headline: S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq close lower on Nov 10 after inflation data
stories.what: The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,520.93, the Dow lost 0.3% to 52,231.89 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.7% to 25,065.87. Traders raised their forecasts for Fed rate hikes after the inflation report, and Treasury yields jumped even as oil kept easing.
stories.why: The Nasdaq fell furthest because long-duration tech shares are the most sensitive to higher yields, so the index losses reflect rate pressure more than company news.

stories.headline: Gold and bitcoin slide as the dollar firms and yields rise
stories.what: Gold lost about 1.3% on the day and fell toward the 4,030 to 4,060 range. Bitcoin dropped toward 73,000 after the hot CPI print. Both moves came as the dollar strengthened and Treasury yields rose.
stories.why: Gold and bitcoin pay no yield, so higher real rates and a stronger dollar make them less attractive, and bitcoin also tends to trade with risk appetite.

stories.headline: Oil keeps easing on reports of possible US-Iran talks
stories.what: Crude prices fell further on Nov 10 as concern eased about a possible US military strike on Iran. Reports of a disputed Iran deal were cited as a driver of the drop in the days before. WTI was near 87.58 on Nov 9, according to an approximate market summary.
stories.why: Lower oil reduces the energy part of inflation and cuts input costs, which helps the case that inflation can cool. Oil is still high, so the offset is modest.

stories.headline: Asian and European markets rise on Nov 10 as Kospi jumps 4.4%
stories.what: South Korea's Kospi snapped a three-day losing streak and ended 4.4% higher. Germany's DAX rose 1.3% and London's FTSE 100 gained 0.4% in the same session.
stories.why: A firm overseas session shows that global risk appetite held up on Nov 10 despite the US rate worries, which may help the US open on Nov 12.

bottomLine: Inflation came in hotter than expected on both headline and core prices, and the Fed is now seen possibly hiking again in December rather than cutting. With the 10-year yield near 5%, rate pressure is weighing most on high-valuation tech, and the AI spending worries that hit megacaps in early November have not gone away. Easing oil prices are the main offset. The Wednesday Nov 11 session is not confirmed in the sources available, so the snapshot reflects the Nov 10 close.
